items.definition: Your neck is the part that holds your head up. You can wear a scarf around it.
items.example: She wore a scarf around her neck.
items.picture_idea: A person with a hand touching the neck between head and shoulders
items.definition_previous: The part of your body between your head and your shoulders.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the part of an organism (human or animal) that connects the head to the rest of the body

items.definition: You say new when something was just made or got. A new bag has not been used for long.
items.example: I have a new bag for school.
items.picture_idea: A shiny new bag with a price tag
items.definition_previous: Not old; made or bought a short time ago.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: not of long duration; having just (or relatively recently) come into being or been made or acquired or discovered

items.definition: Your nose is on your face, above your mouth. You smell things and breathe through it.
items.example: My nose is cold.
items.picture_idea: A smiling face with the nose highlighted
items.definition_previous: The part of your face that you use to smell and breathe.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the organ of smell and entrance to the respiratory tract; the prominent part of the face of man or other mammals

items.definition: You open a door or box by moving it so it is not shut. Say open to ask for this.
items.example: Please open the door.
items.picture_idea: A child opening a door
items.definition_previous: To move something so that it is not closed.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cause to open or to become open

items.definition: Old means something has been around for a long time. An old watch has been used for many years.
items.example: My grandfather has an old watch.
items.picture_idea: An old man holding an old pocket watch
items.definition_previous: Having lived or existed for a long time; not new.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: of long duration; not new

items.definition: Pants are clothes that cover your legs from your waist down. You put one leg in each side.
items.explanation: Always plural. Say 'a pair of pants'. In British English, 'pants' can mean underwear.
items.example: I put on my blue pants.
items.picture_idea: A pair of blue long pants
items.definition_previous: Clothes that cover your legs and waist; trousers.

definition_basis.note: no WordNet meaning fit; written by Claude

items.definition: A park is a big open place outside with grass and trees. People go there to walk and play.
items.example: We play in the park on Sunday.
items.picture_idea: Children playing on grass with trees and a swing
items.definition_previous: A place outside with grass and trees where people can walk and play.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of open land for recreational use in an urban area

items.definition: A pillow is a soft thing you put under your head when you lie down in bed to sleep.
items.example: I put my head on the pillow.
items.picture_idea: A white pillow on a bed
items.definition_previous: A soft thing you put your head on when you sleep.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a cushion to support the head of a sleeping person

items.definition: You play when you do something for fun, like a game with a ball. Say play when you want fun.
items.example: The children play with a ball.
items.picture_idea: Two children kicking a ball
items.definition_previous: To do something for fun, like a game.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be at play; be engaged in playful activity; amuse oneself in a way characteristic of children

items.definition: You pull something by holding it and moving it toward you. Say pull when you want to bring something closer.
items.example: Pull the door to open it.
items.picture_idea: A person pulling a door handle toward them
items.definition_previous: To hold something and move it toward you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: apply force so as to cause motion towards the source of the motion

items.definition: You push something by pressing it so it moves away from you. Say push to move something away.
items.example: Push the box across the floor.
items.picture_idea: A child pushing a large box
items.definition_previous: To press something to make it move away from you.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move with force

items.definition: If a room is quiet, there is very little noise. You can only hear small sounds.
items.example: The baby is sleeping, so please be quiet.
items.picture_idea: A person with a finger on their lips
items.definition_previous: Making very little or no sound.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: free of noise or uproar; or making little if any sound

items.definition: Rain is water that falls from clouds in small drops. You get wet in it if you have no umbrella.
items.explanation: Rain is not usually counted. You can also use 'rain' as a verb: 'It rains a lot here.'
items.example: I do not like walking in the rain.
items.picture_idea: Grey clouds with raindrops falling
items.definition_previous: Water that falls from the clouds in small drops.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: water falling in drops from vapor condensed in the atmosphere

items.definition: You read when you look at words to understand them. Say read when you want to look at a book.
items.explanation: The past form is spelled 'read' but sounds like 'red'.
items.example: I read a book every night.
items.picture_idea: A child reading an open book
items.definition_previous: To look at words and understand them.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: interpret something that is written or printed

items.definition: A room is a space inside a building with walls around it. A house has rooms like a kitchen and a bedroom.
items.example: My room has a small bed and a desk.
items.picture_idea: A small bedroom with a bed and desk
items.definition_previous: A part of a house or building with walls, a floor and a ceiling.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an area within a building enclosed by walls and floor and ceiling

items.definition: You run when you move on your feet very fast. Say run when you want to go faster than walking.
items.example: The dog runs in the garden.
items.picture_idea: A child running across a field
items.definition_previous: To move fast on your feet.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: move fast by using one's feet, with one foot off the ground at any given time

items.definition: You feel sad when something upsets you and you may want to cry. Say sad to tell how you feel.
items.example: He is sad because his friend is moving away.
items.picture_idea: A child with a frown and a tear
items.definition_previous: Feeling unhappy.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: experiencing or showing sorrow or unhappiness

items.definition: A school is a place where children go to learn from teachers. They read, write and count there.
items.example: I walk to school with my sister.
items.picture_idea: A school building with children entering
items.definition_previous: A place where children go to learn.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a building where young people receive education

items.definition: A shirt is clothing you wear on the top half of your body. It has sleeves and often buttons.
items.example: He has a white shirt for school.
items.picture_idea: A white button-up shirt
items.definition_previous: A piece of clothing for the top part of your body, often with buttons.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a garment worn on the upper half of the body

items.definition: A shoe covers your foot when you walk outside. It has a hard bottom to keep your foot safe.
items.explanation: We usually talk about shoes in pairs.
items.example: I cannot find my left shoe.
items.picture_idea: A pair of sneakers
items.definition_previous: Something you wear on your foot when you go outside.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: footwear shaped to fit the foot (below the ankle) with a flexible upper of leather or plastic and a sole and heel of heavier material

items.definition: A shop is a place with things for sale. You pay money for what you want and take it home.
items.example: The shop opens at nine o'clock.
items.picture_idea: A small shop with a sign and a window
items.definition_previous: A place where you buy things.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a mercantile establishment for the retail sale of goods or services

items.definition: Your shoulder is the part of your body between your neck and your arm. You can carry a bag on it.
items.example: My bag is heavy on my shoulder.
items.picture_idea: A person carrying a bag on one shoulder
items.definition_previous: The part of your body where your arm joins your body.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: the part of the body between the neck and the upper arm

items.definition: You sit when your bottom rests on a chair or the floor. Say sit when you want to rest.
items.example: Please sit on the chair.
items.picture_idea: A child sitting on a chair
items.definition_previous: To rest your body on a chair or the floor, not standing.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be in a position in which one's upper body is largely upright and supported by one's backside

items.definition: You sleep when your eyes are closed and your body rests, often at night. Say sleep when you feel tired.
items.example: The baby sleeps in the bedroom.
items.picture_idea: A child sleeping in a bed with closed eyes
items.definition_previous: To rest with your eyes closed and your mind quiet, usually at night.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be asleep

items.definition: A sock is a soft cover you wear on your foot, inside a shoe. It keeps your foot warm.
items.example: I have a hole in my sock.
items.picture_idea: A pair of colorful socks
items.definition_previous: A soft piece of clothing you wear on your foot inside a shoe.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: hosiery consisting of a cloth covering for the foot; worn inside the shoe; reaches to between the ankle and the knee

items.definition: A sofa is a long, soft seat for two or more people. You sit on it at home.
items.example: We watch TV on the sofa.
items.picture_idea: A living room sofa with cushions
items.definition_previous: A long, soft seat for two or more people.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an upholstered seat for more than one person

items.definition: You stand when you are up on your feet, not sitting. Say stand to ask someone to get up.
items.example: Please stand next to the door.
items.picture_idea: A person standing up straight beside a chair
items.definition_previous: To be on your feet, not sitting.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be standing; be upright

items.definition: Stairs are steps that go up or down from one floor to another. You walk on them to change floors.
items.explanation: Usually plural. You can also say 'a staircase'.
items.example: My bedroom is at the top of the stairs.
items.picture_idea: An indoor staircase with a handrail
items.definition_previous: Steps that you use to go up or down inside a building.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a flight of stairs or a flight of steps

items.definition: A table has a flat top and legs. You put food, books, or other things on it.
items.example: We eat dinner at the table.
items.picture_idea: A wooden table with plates and cups
items.definition_previous: A piece of furniture with a flat top and legs.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a piece of furniture having a smooth flat top that is usually supported by one or more vertical legs

items.definition: A tooth is one of the hard white parts in your mouth. You use your teeth to bite and chew food.
items.example: I brush my teeth every morning.
items.picture_idea: A smiling mouth showing white teeth
items.definition_previous: One of the hard white parts in your mouth that you use to bite and chew.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: hard bonelike structures in the jaws of vertebrates; used for biting and chewing or for attack and defense

items.definition: You feel tired when you have no energy and want to rest or sleep. Say tired to tell how you feel.
items.example: I am tired after a long day.
items.picture_idea: A person yawning with heavy eyes
items.definition_previous: Feeling that you need to rest or sleep.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: depleted of strength or energy

items.definition: A toilet is a bowl with a seat. You sit on it to pee or poop, usually in the bathroom.
items.explanation: In American English, people often say 'bathroom' or 'restroom' for the room.
items.example: Where is the toilet, please?
items.picture_idea: A white toilet in a small bathroom
items.definition_previous: A bowl with a seat that you use when you need to pass waste from your body; also the room with this bowl.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a plumbing fixture for defecation and urination

items.definition: A towel is a soft cloth. You use it to dry your body or hands after washing.
items.example: Dry your hands with the towel.
items.picture_idea: A folded blue towel hanging on a rail
items.definition_previous: A soft cloth that you use to dry your body or hands.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a rectangular piece of absorbent cloth (or paper) for drying or wiping

items.definition: An umbrella is a round cover on a stick that you hold over your head. It keeps the rain off you.
items.example: Take an umbrella because it is raining.
items.picture_idea: A person holding an open umbrella in the rain
items.definition_previous: A thing you hold over your head to keep off the rain.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a lightweight handheld collapsible canopy

items.definition: Up means toward a higher place. Say up when someone or something goes higher, like climbing a tree.
items.example: The cat climbed up the tree.
items.picture_idea: An arrow pointing up and a cat climbing a tree
items.definition_previous: In or toward a higher place.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: spatially or metaphorically from a lower to a higher position

items.definition: You walk when you move along on your feet, one step at a time. Say walk when you go somewhere on foot.
items.example: We walk to the shop every day.
items.picture_idea: Two people walking on a path
items.definition_previous: To move on your feet at a normal speed.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: use one's feet to advance; advance by steps

items.definition: A wall is one flat side of a room or building. Pictures and windows can be on a wall.
items.example: There is a picture on the wall.
items.picture_idea: A wall with a framed picture
items.definition_previous: A side of a room or building, or something built to close off a space.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: an architectural partition with a height and length greater than its thickness; used to divide or enclose an area or to support another structure

items.definition: You want something when you would like to have it or do it. Say want to ask for something.
items.example: I want a glass of water.
items.picture_idea: A child pointing at a glass of water
items.definition_previous: To wish to have or do something.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: feel or have a desire for; want strongly

items.definition: Something warm has heat that feels nice, not too hot and not cold. A warm bath feels good.
items.example: The room is warm.
items.picture_idea: A person wrapped in a blanket near a heater
items.definition_previous: A little hot, in a nice way.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: having or producing a comfortable and agreeable degree of heat or imparting or maintaining heat

items.definition: You wash something to get it clean with water and soap. Say wash when something is dirty.
items.example: I wash my hands before dinner.
items.picture_idea: Hands under a running tap with soap
items.definition_previous: To clean something with water and soap.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: cleanse with a cleaning agent, such as soap, and water

items.definition: You wait when you stay in one place until something happens. Say wait to ask someone to stay for now.
items.example: Please wait here for me.
items.picture_idea: A person standing at a bus stop looking at a watch
items.definition_previous: To stay in a place until something happens.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: stay in one place and anticipate or expect something

items.definition: You wear clothes when you have them on your body. You wear a coat when it is cold.
items.example: She wears a red coat in winter.
items.picture_idea: A girl in a red coat and hat
items.definition_previous: To have clothes or shoes on your body.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: be dressed in

items.definition: A window is an opening in a wall with glass in it. You look through it to see outside.
items.example: Open the window, please.
items.picture_idea: A house window with a view of trees
items.definition_previous: An opening in a wall with glass, so you can see outside.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a framework of wood or metal that contains a glass windowpane and is built into a wall or roof to admit light or air

items.definition: You feel worried when you think something bad might happen. Your mind keeps thinking about it.
items.example: Mom is worried because I am late.
items.picture_idea: A person with a frown biting their nails
items.definition_previous: Feeling that something bad may happen.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: mentally upset over possible misfortune or danger etc

items.definition: You write when you make letters or words on paper or on a screen, with a pen or keys.
items.example: I write my name on the paper.
items.picture_idea: A child writing with a pencil on paper
items.definition_previous: To make letters or words on paper or a screen.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: mark or trace words or symbols on a surface

items.definition: You means the person or people you are talking to. Say you when you speak to them.
items.example: Can you help me?
items.picture_idea: One person pointing toward the viewer
items.definition_previous: The person or people I am talking to.

definition_basis.note: WordNet has no entry for this word; written by Claude

items.definition: A zipper closes a coat or bag. You pull a small tab, and the two sides lock together.
items.explanation: In British English, it is often called a 'zip'.
items.example: The zipper on my coat is stuck.
items.picture_idea: A close-up of a zipper on a jacket
items.definition_previous: A thing on clothes or bags that closes two sides by pulling a small tab.

definition_basis.wordnet_meaning: a fastener for locking together two toothed edges by means of a sliding tab
